body:
Maintainer ruling (2026-08-18, live PM chat with the triage seat, session `session_01EUZUjvnLsqwHVkXkTv8TKQ`; verbatim: 「其他接受你的建议」, applying the triage recommendation delivered for this card).

**Ruled: `properties` wins on BOTH channels — one answer per key.** The canonical spelling's precedence must hold on the React-prop channel too (today `...(evaluatedSchema.props || {})` spreads last and inverts it); the config-bag channel's `properties`-wins order is already correct and stays. This restores the declared posture (`props` is annotated legacy alias) rather than changing it.

Dispatch requirements: (1) before the fix, scan the repo + examples for nodes carrying BOTH spellings and attach the count — any real co-occurrence sites get called out in the PR since their rendered output may change; (2) pin the invariant cross-channel (same key, both read paths, one winner) so the inversion cannot regrow; (3) note the adjacency to #4795's pending question ② (whether the `properties` envelope is an official ui:* authoring channel) — this ruling fixes precedence, it does not answer that. Promoted to `pm:queue` (type stays Bug).

**Deferred this round — recording the reason and the trap now rather than when it comes up again** (deferring is not shelving).

**Why deferred**: this card's fix surface is `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` + `packages/components/src/renderers/basic/elements.tsx`. **#5253 is in flight in `packages/components`** (`src/renderers/form/form.tsx`). The maintainer's 2026-08-18 subdirectory/file-level serialization exemption is **app-shell-only and ⛔ does not extend to `packages/components`**, so whole-package serialization applies and these two cannot run concurrently. Not a judgement on the card — purely the queue.

**The trap the next dispatch needs to know about**, so it is not rediscovered:

The two channels disagree in **opposite directions**, and the fix is not "pick one spelling" —

| channel | precedence | site |
|---|---|---|
| config bag (`schema.properties.x`) | **`properties` wins** | `readProps()` = `{ ...schema.props, ...schema.properties }` |
| React prop (`x` arriving as a prop) | **`props` wins** | `SchemaRenderer`'s `createElement`: `...componentProps` first, then `...(evaluatedSchema.props \|\| {})` overwrites |

So whichever way you unify it, **one of the two currently-working readings changes behaviour**. The `readProps()` family is five named files (`elements.tsx`, `text-input.tsx`, `record-picker.tsx`, `data-list.tsx`, `metadata-viewer.tsx`); everything else takes the spread path. That asymmetry is why this is not a one-line alias fix and why it wants its ruling read before dispatch, not during.

Also relevant to whoever picks it up: **PR #5122 (#4799) neither introduced nor changed this** — it explicitly preserved `readProps`'s `properties` precedence. So the card's premise is not a side effect of that merge, but the tree has moved since 2026-08-18 02:22 and the spread order at `createElement` must be re-read on current `main` rather than trusted from this body.

Still `pm:queue`, unassigned, no label change.

Clause-②: **no** — the maintainer's ruling frames this as *restoring* the declared posture (`props` is an annotated legacy alias), not changing it. No key gains or loses acceptance; only which of two co-present spellings wins. Flagging it here because it is the closest call of this round: the **rendered output can change** for any node that writes both, which is exactly why requirement (1) below is a hard pre-condition rather than a nicety.
Serial constraints cleared: **the blocker named in my deferral comment above is gone.** `packages/components` was held by #5253; its PR #5276 **merged**, so the package is free. `packages/react` was never held. The three other in-flight cards are in `packages/plugin-report` (#5225), `packages/core` + `plugin-charts` (#4507), and `apps/console` (#4303) — all disjoint. Open PRs #5277 (`packages/fields`) and #5278 (`app-shell/src/providers`) likewise disjoint.

The maintainer's ruling and its **three binding dispatch requirements** are carried into the order verbatim — in particular requirement (1): **count the co-occurrence sites before touching the fix**, because those are the nodes whose rendered output this change can alter, and an unmeasured zero there is not a reading.

### Requirement (1) — the co-occurrence measurement, with its counter-probe

The ruling made this a pre-condition, so recording the numbers here as well as in the PR. Method: `JSON.parse` + recursive object walk for every `.json`; a brace-depth, string- and comment-aware object-literal scan for every `.ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.mjs/.md/.mdx`. Both passes validated against a positive control (a synthetic node written both ways) — both detected it, so the detector is not dead.

| corpus | files parsed | nodes with BOTH | only `props` | only `properties` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `examples/` (JSON) | 432 | **0** | 0 | 0 |
| whole repo (JSON) | 546 | **0** | 1 | 2 |
| whole repo (source literals) | 3924 scanned | **1** (test fixture) | — | — |

**Counter-probe** — the zeros are readings, not an empty scan:

- `examples/`: the same walk parsed **2277 `"type"` keys across 428 files**. That corpus authors config **flat on the node** (`{ "type": "statistic", "label": …, "value": … }`) and contains **zero** occurrences of either spelling as a key — so the zero there is structural, not a miss.
- Whole repo: 800 files contain `props`, 344 contain `properties`, 12 contain `readProps`; 3 JSON nodes carry exactly one of the two spellings; 28 non-test source literals declare a `properties:` bag against 1 declaring a `props:` bag.

**Blast radius: no authored site changes rendered output.** The one co-occurrence node in the repo is `packages/react/src/__tests__/SchemaRenderer.propertiesExpressions.test.tsx` (the objectui#4799 pin). Its output does not move — it asserts the config-bag read, which this change deliberately leaves alone — and it passes unmodified in the full run above. The dispatch's honest risk ("one of the two currently-working readings changes behaviour") therefore lands on **no existing site**, which is why this did not need the stop-and-report escalation.

### Notes for the PM

- **A sixth `readProps()` implementation exists on current `main`** — `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-alert.tsx`, `{ ...schema, ...schema.properties }`. Not one of the five named in the deferral comment. It already agrees with the ruling (`properties` wins), so it needed no edit, but the "five named files" list is now stale and worth correcting wherever it is carried forward.
- PR #5284 is **draft**, `Fixes #5123`. Labels applied by the bot and read back: `package: react`, `package: components`, `tests`. No `skip-changeset` label was created or applied — this PR ships a real changeset, and per the dispatch that label mechanism does not exist in this repo.
- Base `main` advanced during the run (branched at `97fba31a2`, PR base now `92b327a67`). CI convergence is left to the PM per the 2026-08-10 ruling; report delivered at draft-PR time, no CI polling.

**ACCEPT** — PR #5284 flipped ready, enqueued, merged. All 21 checks resolved: 19 success, 2 skipped by design.

**Requirement (1), the maintainer's hard pre-condition, came back zero — and it is the right kind of zero.** No node in shipped metadata or source carries both spellings. The single co-occurrence site in the whole repo is #4799's test fixture, and its rendered output does **not** change (it asserts the *bag* read, which this PR leaves alone); it passes unmodified. So the blast radius the ruling was guarding against is genuinely empty here.

**Requirement (2)** is pinned the way a cross-channel invariant has to be: the central assertion is an **equality between channels** — `expect(bagRead).toBe(reactPropRead)` — so re-inverting either side fails even if someone later edits the per-channel expectations. 12 tests across two files. **Requirement (3)**: #4795's question ② is untouched and explicitly not answered, in the PR body and both test files.

Three things here are better than what my dispatch order asked for:

1. **It avoided a regression neither the ruling nor I anticipated.** The obvious way to make `properties` win on the React-prop channel is to re-spread `properties` *after* `props`. That would have been wrong: `properties.*` is **already** in `componentProps`, having passed the metadata strip — re-spreading the raw bag would push stripped metadata (e.g. `dataSource`) back out as React props, which is the **objectstack#5576** regression. It implemented the fix as a **subtraction** from the props bag instead.

2. **A sixth `readProps()` family member exists, and it was checked.** My order said the family was five named files and that a sixth would matter. `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-alert.tsx` merges `{ ...schema, ...schema.properties }` — a different expression of the same properties-wins order, so it already agrees with the ruling and needed no change. Verified, not assumed.

3. **The ablation proved dist was not in the resolution path rather than asserting it.** It ran with `packages/react/dist/SchemaRenderer.js` **still containing the fixed build** (2 occurrences of the new helper in dist while src had 0) and went red anyway. A stale artifact in the path would have produced a false **green** — so this is a positive control, not a claim. Predicted 5 of 12 red by name; observed exactly those 5.

The pre-fix measurement also reproduced the card's original probe exactly — `bagRead='FROM_PROPERTIES'` while `reactPropRead='FROM_PROPS'` — so the defect this closes is the one that was filed.
